newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa braced for one hour national stoppage.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa braced for one hour national stoppage.

text.p: South Africa on Monday was braced for a national one hour work stoppage called by the country's biggest labour group, the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu).
At the centre of the current controversy is the new Basic Conditions of Employment Bill which has been approved by Cabinet and is due to be tabled in parliament by September 15.
"We are still going ahead with the stoppages...At the moment we expect all two million members of Costau to join in," a Cosatu spokeswoman told Reuters.
Cosatu affiliated unions are organised in major sectors including mining, metal and engineering, chemical and oil, motor industry and health and transport as well as the public sector.
Cosatu is in alliance with the ruling African National Congress (ANC) of President Nelson Mandela, but the left-leaning labour group has been disappointed by Mandela's market-friendly policies.

Cosatu first sought to flex its political muscle with a national one-day strike on June 2 to drive home its core demands for six months' maternity leave, of which at least four should be paid, and a 40-hour working week to be phased in over five years.
Monday's stoppage will be followed by 24-hour strikes in all the major regions in the country from August 18 to August 21 -- unless agreement is reached before then.
Business objects to the two core demands, arguing that certain of the provisions in the bill could raise employment costs to the point of creating obstacles to new jobs.
